newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban holds off Masood forces at Afghan pass.
newsitem.headline: Taleban holds off Masood forces at Afghan pass.

text.p: Taleban troops held on to a strategic pass north of Kabul on Sunday despite an assault by ousted Afghan government forces using rockets, artillery and warplanes to try and dislodge them.
Fighting died down in the afternoon but intermittent shells and rockets could still be seen landing on the De Sabz pass, about 30 km (20 miles) north of the Afghan capital.
Asked if former government forces under ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood had taken the pass, Masood's spokesman, Doctor Abdullah, said: "No, not yet."

Abdullah spoke at a mud-walled compound in Tutakhon, back from the De Sabz pass, where the attack was being lead by General Abdul Rauf Begi, a commander belonging to forces of the northern Uzbek leader, General Abdul Rashid Dostum.

Masood's former government's forces have allied with Dostum's in a bid to drive the radical Islamic Taleban militia out of Kabul. The Taleban captured the city one month ago on Sunday giving it control of over two-thirds of the country.
Forces belonging to the alliance are ranged out on highly exposed ground below the pass, hindering a push forward, former government commanders said.
